newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt slips, issuance steps up.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt slips, issuance steps up.

text.p: Emerging market debt gave up early firmess when the U.S. Treasuries turned down.
Trading was range-bound in light volume, traders said.

"It's squaring up time," said a Brady bond trader. The March producer price index and march retail sales have been closely watched for signs of exceptional vigor that might further stoke inflationary fears.
Players stayed mainly on the more liquid issues, such as Arg FRB and Brazil C, with no particular preference for floaters, or fixed rate bonds, the trader said.
Argentina FRBs eased 1/8 to 89-5/8 bid. Brazil C lost 3/8 to 74-7/8 bid.
Compared with the subdued secondary trading, primary issuance picked up with a vengence.
Mexico issued a five-year 100 billion yen samurai bond, the fifth in just over a year.
Argentina launched an one billion Austrian shilling bond, that is fungible with its mark denominated bond issued in February. The country is also planning a 500 bilion lire seven-year issue.

Also in the pipeline is Brazil's "parallel bond", which is likely denominated in one or more core European currencies with a redenomination clause into euros if European Economic and Monetary Union goes ahead.
"They want to tap into other OECD countries before global liquidity dries up," said an analyst who declined to be named.
All non-dollar proceeds are usually swapped into dollars.

Ecuador is plugging its eurobond in a roadshow in New York. The five-year issue, up to $400 million, has met with quite a lot of skepticism, given the political turmoil in Ecuador, market sources said.
"Ecuador does not have a compelling story to tell investors at this point," said the analyst. "The situation is not getting worse, but hardly getting any better."

The interim president, Fabian Alarcon, last week called a popular vote to reaffirm the legitimacy of his government. Alarcon assumed the presidency after Abdala Bucaram was outsted in early February. His mandate expires in August 1998.

On the economic front in Ecuador, the drop in world oil prices more than offset any benefit from rising banana exports, the analyst said. Oil and banana are the country's two leading export commodities.
Ecuador was seen under strong pressure to issue the eurobond to repay the bridge loan it owed even the market condition was hardly favorable, said a trader.
Ecuador PDI was off 1/4 at 55-1/2 bid.
Year-to-date, while JP morgan's emerging market composite index still showed a 1.11 percent gain, the Ecuador subindex lost 6.94 percent.
